description: An eight-panel composite figure combining four bright-field TEM micrographs (a–d) with four precession-based ACOM maps (e–h), all from tensile specimens deformed to true strain ≈0.015. (a) 28Mn0Ni: sparse curved dislocations with only isolated pinning, scale bar printed "200 μm". (b) 15Mn5Ni, ZA: [011]Al||[111]B2: dense dislocation accumulation in the austenite channels between carbide particles, scale bar printed "500 μm". (c) a γ/B2 interface where slip transfer is marked by red arrows, with an SAED inset (10 nm⁻¹, single-crystal spot pattern) confirming the orientation relationship, scale bar "200 μm". (d) region showing slip restriction at a B2/B2 interface, scale bar 1 μm. (e) ACOM virtual bright-field of a region containing γ grains plus a B2 stringer labelled f-B2 (favourable OR) and nf-B2 (non-favourable OR), ZA: [011]Al||[111]B2, 3 μm scale bar. (f) coloured IPF orientation map with a 001/101/111 colour triangle inset. (g) phase map: red = γ, blue = B2 stringer. (h) KAM map with colour scale Min 0 – Max 5, dashed arrows marking slip transfer across f-B2 and solid arrows marking strain accumulation around nf-B2. Together the panels argue that γ/B2 interfaces with a favourable OR transmit slip so γ and B2 deform as a composite, whereas hard-oriented B2 grains accumulate local strain that later nucleates cracks.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of 28Mn0Ni deformed near yield (ε≈0.015); widely spaced curved individual dislocations with sparse pinning, uniform light-grey contrast. Scale bar printed '200 μm'.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of 15Mn5Ni deformed to the same strain; top annotation reads 'ZA: [011]Al||[111]B2'. Dense dark dislocation tangles fill austenite channels between lighter carbide particles. Scale bar printed '500 μm'.

Bright-field TEM of a γ/B2 interface; two red arrows point to slip bands crossing the interface. Inset bottom-right is an SAED pattern (scale '10 nm⁻¹') showing a single-crystal spot pattern consistent with a specific orientation relationship.
Bright-field TEM of a B2/B2 interface with adjacent grains of differing contrast; slip bands stop at the boundary (slip restriction), several inclined bands visible. Scale bar 1 μm.

ACOM virtual bright-field image with annotation 'ZA: [011]Al||[111]B2'. A B2 stringer region is labelled 'f-B2' and an adjacent B2 particle is labelled 'nf-B2' on a γ matrix background. Scale bar 3 μm.
Coloured inverse-pole-figure orientation map of the same region; grains coloured in pink/red, blue/violet, green, orange. Bottom-right inset is the 001/101/111 IPF colour triangle. Scale bar 3 μm.
Phase map of the same region: red = γ (dominant), blue = B2 forming a diagonal stringer plus a separate rounded B2 particle. Legend bottom-right: red 'γ', blue 'B2'. Scale bar 3 μm.

KAM map of the same region using a green-to-blue/red colour scale labelled 'Min 0' to 'Max 5'. Two dashed white arrows on the left mark slip transfer across the f-B2 stringer; two solid white arrows on the right mark high-misorientation strain accumulation around the nf-B2 particle. Scale bar 3 μm.

observations.observation: Panel (a) (28Mn0Ni, deformed near yield) shows only sparse, widely separated curved dislocations with isolated pinning; no dense dislocation tangles are visible.
Panel (b) (15Mn5Ni, same applied strain) shows dense dislocation accumulation confined to the austenite channels between carbide particles, and is annotated 'ZA: [011]Al||[111]B2'.
Panel (c) marks slip transfer across a γ/B2 interface with two red arrows and contains an SAED inset with the scale '10 nm⁻¹' showing a discrete single-crystal spot pattern.
Panel (d) shows a B2/B2 interface at which slip bands terminate rather than cross, i.e. slip restriction, with a 1 μm scale bar.
Panel (e) labels two B2 regions in the ACOM virtual bright-field: 'f-B2' (favourable orientation relationship) and 'nf-B2' (non-favourable orientation relationship).
Panel (g) is a phase map with legend red = γ and blue = B2, showing the B2 stringer as a continuous diagonal band plus a separate rounded B2 particle embedded in the γ matrix.

Panel (h) is a KAM map with a colour bar labelled 'Min 0' to 'Max 5'; dashed white arrows mark slip transfer across f-B2 while solid white arrows mark localised high-misorientation strain accumulation around nf-B2.
Panel (f) is an IPF orientation map with a 001/101/111 colour triangle inset, showing grains of contrasting orientations including the B2 stringer region.
The caption states panels (a) and (b) are bright-field TEM micrographs of 28Mn0Ni and 15Mn5Ni respectively, deformed near the yield point.
The citing text asserts that slip transfer at the γ/B2 interface implies substantial load sharing between the phases, i.e. composite yielding.
The citing text states that slip transfer was not observed across all γ/B2 interfaces around a single B2 stringer, so γ-matrix and B2 grains can deform simultaneously near yield.

The citing text reports that the KAM map highlights traces of slip transfer across interfaces of the B2 stringer where the OR exists, but substantial strain accumulation where the OR is absent ('nf-B2', hard orientations).

The citing text attributes the higher yield strength of 15Mn5Ni versus 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni to a large fraction of coarser carbides, a bamboo-like B2 stringer morphology with fine DO3 ordered precipitates, and restricted slip across non-favourable γ/B2 interfaces.
The ACOM analysis was performed on a 15Mn5Ni tensile specimen deformed to ε≈0.015, with about ten such regions examined (citing text).

measured_quantities: kernel average misorientation, KAM (degrees, colour scale Min 0 – Max 5)
SAED camera length scale (nm⁻¹, inset 10 nm⁻¹)
unreadable_items: Panels (a)–(c) scale bars are printed in μm ('200 μm', '500 μm', '200 μm') although they are TEM micrographs where nm would be expected — read exactly as printed; possible typographic error in the original figure.
The carbide phase label in the caption is rendered as '??-carbide' (garbled, likely κ-carbide); the phase symbol itself cannot be confirmed from the pixels.
Panel (c) inset SAED spot indices are not labelled; only the pattern and its 10 nm⁻¹ scale are readable.
Colour-bar intermediate tick values in panel (h) beyond Min 0 and Max 5 are unreadable.
